gate0.note:
GATE 0: idea-01 Ledger. Human decision. The reason given on the pick line ('event log fold, state never stored') described idea-02 Dispatch; the human confirmed Ledger was intended, so no rationale is recorded beyond the choice itself.

CARRY TO GATE 1 - the idea's own two stated risks:
  1. Session 2 is thin if it is only a sum. The running-balance column and the
     file-order rule are what make it worth 40 minutes and must be graded
     separately from the per-account total.
  2. The parser grammar sprawls. The accepted line shape and the closed list of
     rejection reasons must be stated up front with each reason's exact string,
     or the Verifier grades wording the Builder invented.
  3. Paise conversion needs a fixture with a .05 on it.

gate1.note:
GATE 1 APPROVED - round 2. Human decision; the stopping rule was approve-eligible on its own (no --override).

RULE: 2 blocking, 0 of them owned by 'nothing', 5 worth a look. Linter 0 errors / 0 warnings. 9 criteria, 9 distinct tests, no test shared between two criteria, red-first static clean with no report written. ambiguity.md, lint.json and breaker-begin.json all bound to spec hash 46b5465b4952 with no drift; breaker end confirmed the spec did not move during the pass.

ROUND 1'S TWO BLOCKERS ARE CLOSED, AND CHECKED RATHER THAN ASSERTED. The Breaker re-derived the cut-to-criterion join in both directions: every criterion fails when any one declared cut is emptied alone, no proper subset of a criterion's cuts satisfies it, no two cuts carry the same criterion set, and every cut has more than one grading fixture. A1 (cut-amount-paise bypassable with all nine criteria green) and A2 (account-total's undeclared dependency) are both gone. The arithmetic was recomputed independently for the second time - 30 lines, 3 skipped, 21 accepted, 6 rejected, four account totals, both running columns, all five c-1-3 paise values - with no disagreement.

BOTH REMAINING BLOCKERS SIT IN A DOWNSTREAM CHECKER'S COLUMN:

  B1 (owner: test-runner) - notFound() throws, so the page cannot also render
     account-missing; the element has to live in a not-found.tsx boundary the
     spec never names. No shipped project in this repo has done a real HTTP 404
     on a page route, so there is no house pattern to copy. c-2-4 pins both the
     404 status and the element, so a Builder who gets this wrong produces a red
     test at step 6 rather than a silent defect. Accepted on that basis.

  B2 (owner: typecheck) - with cut-parse-line removed, nothing assigns to
     'reason' between its BAD_FIELDS initialiser and the 'reason === null'
     guard, so TS narrows it to string and the comparison is dead (TS2367).
     This is the TS2355 failure mode arriving through a comparison instead of a
     missing return.

     WATCH AT STEP 10, DO NOT ASSUME THIS IS OWNED. The Breaker's own note is
     that typecheck is the fail-open second-line check. A fail-open owner passes
     when it cannot run, which is the one way a blocking finding in an owned
     column still reaches the skeleton. Read typecheck_fail_open in
     skeleton-check.json and require it false. pipeline-test-02 recorded false;
     anything else means B2 was never actually checked.

ACCEPTED WITH EYES OPEN - THE TIMING, WHICH IS THE ONE THING NEITHER ROUND FIXED:

  Both sessions estimate 38.5 against the 40 cap. The linter is silent because
  every cut sits under the 55-word nominal and is priced at the flat 6.0
  minutes. The Spec Breaker independently reached the same worry in both rounds
  and put it plainly: the model was 12.5 and 13 minutes low on the only two
  flow-2 sessions that have ever been timed (32.5 estimated / 45 measured, and
  37 estimated / 50 measured), and the drop candidates available inside these
  sessions are worth about a minute each against that error bar.

  Shipping anyway is the decision, because the alternative is to reject a spec
  the rule approves on a model I already know to be uncalibrated in this range.
  But the estimate is NOT evidence the sessions fit. Nothing before step 13
  measures teaching minutes, and step 13 is the test.

  PREDICTION ON RECORD, for the dry run to settle: if session 2 runs near 50 on
  a 38.5 estimate, the weighted model is wrong in a way hint length cannot fix,
  and the weight has to move to a quantity the writer does not author.

ON HINT LENGTH: this round's brief told the writer explicitly not to tune hint
length to the nominal. Across five cuts the lengths moved by one word in total
(54->53, the rest unchanged). That argues the lengths are honest rather than
managed - but the same brief also said keep what was not faulted, so the two
explanations are not separable here. Not treated as settled either way.

FIVE WORTH A LOOK, ALL RECORDED AND NONE BLOCKING: W1 new Date('2026-02-30')
rolls to 2 March so that pair discriminates nothing; W2 'never through a float'
is ungraded because Math.round(parseFloat*100) returns all five pinned values;
W3 c-2-4's dependency on cut-account-totals is unobservable since a rows-sum
gives the same number - c-2-5's account-list-total-food is the only observable
read; W4 five specified elements no criterion reads; W5 the drop candidates
above.

gate2.note:
GATE 2 APPROVED. Human decision, pre-authorised after B8 was fixed. Read as every criterion, not as a summary.

RESULTS: 9 pass, 0 fail, 0 skip, 0 missing, pytest rc 0. Session 1 c-1-1..c-1-4 and session 2 c-2-1..c-2-5 all green. Built first pass - no builder/test-runner loop.

MUTATION: 5 of 5 tasks checked, 0 ungraded, 0 inconclusive, stayed_green empty for every cut. For every cut the set that went red equals the set that grades it:
  cut-parse-line        9 lines -> all 9 criteria
  cut-account-totals    7 lines -> c-2-1 c-2-2 c-2-3 c-2-4 c-2-5
  cut-amount-paise      5 lines -> 8 criteria
  cut-running-balance   5 lines -> c-2-3 c-2-5
  cut-account-rows      4 lines -> c-2-3 c-2-4 c-2-5

THE MUTATION RESULT REQUIRED A CHECKER FIX, AND THAT IS PART OF THIS GATE'S RECORD. cut-parse-line first came back INCONCLUSIVE and stopped the phase. It is declared by all nine criteria, so its expected set IS the suite and no criterion could stay green to prove the harness was alive - the per-mutant test, whether any criterion passed, can never be true for that shape. The junit showed tests=9 failures=9 errors=0, so the suite plainly ran. mutation.py now takes the harness-alive control from the run instead of the mutant, requiring both that another mutant produced a pass and that this mutant reported real per-test outcomes. Committed at 8aad102 with 8 selftest checks including both historical false-green shapes.

GATE 1's B1 DID NOT MATERIALISE: the Builder handled notFound() correctly and c-2-4 is green on both the 404 status and the account-missing element. The finding was real and the Builder simply got it right.

RULE 3, STATED PRECISELY RATHER THAN CLAIMED: spec-status reports drift null, still frozen at 46b5465b4952, so the Builder edited neither the spec nor - per the LOCK discipline - the tests. But verify/ is NOT byte-identical to the Gate 1 commit 076a6fa, and that is worth recording rather than glossing:

  verify/helpers.py text_of() gained an explicit timeout=LOAD_TIMEOUT on
  text_content(), plus a docstring. Made at step 8 by the Verifier, which owns
  verify/ in flow 2 and held the lock for it. No assertion was weakened and no
  expected value changed; a missing element now fails on the suite's own 20s
  budget instead of Playwright's hidden 30s default, which is strictly better
  for the skeleton check at step 10 where missing elements are the norm.

  Noting the difference from pipeline-test-02, whose Gate 2 could say verify/
  was byte-identical to its Gate 1 commit. Flow 2 lets the Verifier touch verify/
  at step 8, so 'byte-identical' is not a property this gate can assume; what it
  can check is that every change is the Verifier's and weakens nothing. Checked
  by reading the diff, which is nine lines.

TWO PIPELINE FAULTS BURNED CODE RETRIES 2/15, NEITHER ABOUT THIS PROJECT: the mutation inconclusive above, and a PermissionError from 12 orphaned node servers left by an earlier run (test_runner terminated npm and orphaned its next child). Both fixed at 8aad102; the server leak was verified fixed by measurement - a boot on the leaking path now leaves 0 processes where it left 2. _checker labelled both correctly as pipeline faults supporting no conclusion, which is the hardening working.

STILL OPEN FOR GATE 3:
  - B2 typecheck_fail_open MUST read false in skeleton-check.json. typecheck is
    the fail-open second-line check, and a fail-open owner passes when it cannot
    run. If it reads true, B2 was never actually checked and the TS2367 dead
    comparison reaches the skeleton.
  - TIMING. Both sessions estimate 38.5 against the 40 cap on a model that ran
    12.5 and 13 minutes low on the only two timed flow-2 sessions. The Spec
    Breaker raised it independently in both Gate 1 rounds. The step 13 dry run is
    the test, and the prediction on record is that near-50 means the weight has
    to move off hint length to a quantity the spec writer does not author.

gate3.note:
GATE 3 APPROVED. Human decision, made with the timing in front of it.

THE GATE'S QUESTION IS ANSWERED YES, WITH EVIDENCE. Priya, who did not build this
project, taught session 1 on 2026-09-01 from pack/session-1.md alone, without
opening app/. taught_without_the_code true. That is what Gate 3 asks and it is
answered by a measurement rather than an opinion.

THE TIMING, AND THIS TIME THE DECISIVE FACT IS KNOWN. Session 1 measured 47
minutes against the 40 minute cap - 7 over, and 1 UNDER the guide's own disclosed
estimate of 48. THE TRIMS WERE NOT PULLED. 47 is therefore the cost of teaching
the plan in full, not the cost of the session as the guide intends it taught.

The guide names three trims for session 1 - the npm ci moved before the session,
both regexes handed over pre-written at minute 14, and the rule-order argument
deferred to session 2's recap - and prices them as bringing the session to 40.
Nothing in this measurement contradicts that. It establishes the untrimmed
ceiling and leaves the trimmed plan untested.

This is the answer the last two dry runs could not give. pipeline-test-02 shipped
at 50 against 40 without knowing whether its levers had been pulled, so its
overrun could not be told apart from a session taught long. Here it can:
the plan is not too big, it was taught in full.

WHAT AN INSTRUCTOR MUST BE TOLD BEFORE THEY SCHEDULE THIS: session 1 runs 47
minutes taught complete. To fit 40, pull the three trims the guide names - they
are real live minutes, unlike the drop candidates the SPEC named, which were
markup no student types (ambiguity W5, caught by the Pack Writer). Teaching it
untrimmed is a legitimate choice; it just needs 47 minutes on the timetable.

HANDOVER CHECKS ALL GREEN: cut ran first pass, 5 cuts, 0 retries. Leak scan clean,
0 leaks. Guide lint 0 errors, 2 warnings, both the intended G032 overrun
disclosures. Deploy ok, 0 advisories. skeleton-check 9 checked, 0 mismatches, 0
partial-state risks, and typecheck_fail_open FALSE - so Gate 1's B2, the TS2367
dead comparison whose only owner could have passed by failing to run, was
genuinely checked rather than merely owned.

WHAT THIS RUN TAUGHT THE PIPELINE, RECORDED HERE BECAUSE THE PROJECT IS THE
SMALLER HALF OF IT. Nine defects found, six of them in the pipeline rather than
the project: workflows crashing with a TypeError instead of naming the checker
that did not run; the mutation check unable to reach a verdict on a cut every
criterion declares; two separate sites leaking a server per boot; the phase-2
workflow reporting an inconclusive result as ungraded and printing an instruction
to reject a Gate-1-approved spec; and nothing at all checking whether the test
suite Gate 1 approved was the suite that graded the code. All fixed, each with a
selftest check. Selftest 318 -> 363 across the run.

THE ESTIMATE, SCORED HONESTLY. Three predictions were on record before session 1
ran: the Pack Writer said 48, the new decision-count linter model said 52.1, the
old flat model said 38.5. Measured 47. The linter model beat the flat one and
lost to the Pack Writer by five times, which is the expected result - the Pack
Writer reads the session plan it has just written, the linter reads prose in
spec.json before a plan exists. Constants were NOT refitted on this point: doing
so moves the worst error 5.1 to 4.9, which is noise.

FIVE PROJECTS, FIVE SESSIONS OVER THE CAP - 45, 45, 45, 50, 47. Every fix so far
has argued about how wrong the estimate is. This is the first run where the guide
named trims that are real and a dry run said whether they were used. The next
lever is not a better estimate; it is confirming that a trimmed session actually
lands at 40, which needs one more dry run of session 1 WITH the trims pulled.

dry_run.note:
Session 1 taught from pack/session-1.md by Priya, who did not build it, without opening app/. Measured 47 minutes against the 40 minute cap, and 1 under the guide's own disclosed estimate of 48.

TRIMS WERE NOT PULLED. 47 is the cost of teaching the plan in full. The guide names three trims for this session - pre-session npm ci, both regexes handed over pre-written at minute 14, and the rule-order argument deferred to session 2's recap - and prices them as bringing session 1 to 40. So the 40 minute plan holds WITH the trims and this measurement does not contradict it; it measures the untrimmed ceiling.

This is the answer pipeline-test-02's dry run could not give, and it is the difference between 'the plan is too big' and 'the plan was taught long'. It is the latter.
